body.zh-HK:
> 面試官問：一個 long-context assistant 間中 memory 爆滿。有人提議將 KV cache 清得更勤力；另一個人說應該將 context 上限加大，因為用戶不想被截斷。你會怎樣設計 capacity contract？
>
> 答啱一半嘅答案：KV cache 會食 memory，所以將舊 cache 刪掉；如果有人真的要長 context，再加大 GPU memory。

這個答案知道 memory 是瓶頸，卻把 cache 當成垃圾桶。**KV cache** 保存 attention 在已讀 token 上算出的 key 和 value，讓 model decode 下一個 token 時不用把整段 context 每次由頭重算。它換來速度，也意味每個仍在服務中的長 request 佔著 device memory。儲量會隨 token、layer、head size、precision 和同時活躍 session 增加；所以不是「cache 有沒有」，而是「每種 request 可以預留多少、幾時不准進來」。

## 先承諾可用容量

capacity contract 不是一句「最多 N 個 users」。它是能被 scheduler 執行的承諾：model weight 留多少 memory、每類 request 估算多少 input token 加上可預留 output token、正常負載下要留多少 headroom、哪些 session 可以 idle expiry、哪些 active decode 不可被驅逐、以及 admission 失敗後去什麼 route。沒有 output reservation 的 admission 容易騙過自己：request 一開始進得去，生成途中才 OOM，還可能拖垮已在回答的人。

先把 request 分開，例如短互動、長文件摘要、可恢復 batch job。每類有 context cap、最大 output、deadline 和可接受的替代路徑。長文件不是天然值得吃掉所有 memory；若它可非同步完成，應該入等候隊列或用較小 context 分段處理。反過來，若是已開始的真人互動 decode，隨便 eviction 會令答案中途消失，造成比「請稍後」更差的體驗。

想像圖書館的讀書桌。每位讀者攤開的書、筆記和電腦都需要桌面，這像 active KV cache。把未離座的人東西扔掉，桌子很快騰出來，但讀者回來要從頭整理，而且可能已經失去工作；無限制地讓人堆滿資料，最後新讀者連坐下也做不到。管理者需要預約位、保留的空桌、離座期限和清楚的候補安排。

## 將估算變成 admission 規則

先量一份 synthetic memory ledger：可用 device memory、model weight、runtime overhead、每類 token bucket 的預估 KV 需求，以及剩下 headroom。每條 request 入隊時，以 input token 和保留的 maximum output token 做保守估算；足夠才 admission。不足時不要硬塞：可縮小 context、排隊、轉 async、提供已知的 baseline 回覆，或交給人工流程。這些路徑必須在 trace 裡看得見。

再測三種壓力：很多中等 session 同時 decode、一條極長文件突然到達、idle session 恰好在高峰回來。記錄 admission reject、queue time、eviction、OOM、cancel、恢復成本、TTFT 和完整率。你要的不是「從沒 full」，而是 active session 沒被無故打斷，拒絕有明確原因，並且發生壓力時仍留有 rollback path。

## 容易被忽略的界線

較低 precision、paging 或更聰明的 cache manager 都可能改善容量，卻不是 capacity contract 的替代品。量化可能改輸出品質；paging 可能改 tail latency；eviction policy 可能把慢問題轉成重算問題。若未定 input/output cap、headroom 同 reject/handoff 規則，任何技巧都只是推遲下一次 OOM。這就是為何「加硬件」不是第一句，而是 trace 證實什麼部分需要擴張後的一個選項。

## 可以放進 portfolio 的可檢查 artefact

建立 `kv-cache-capacity-contract`：

- `fixtures/sessions.jsonl`：虛構 session 的 token bucket、deadline、是否可 async 和 expected output cap。
- `scripts/estimate-capacity.mjs`：用明確假設輸出 reservation、headroom 和 admission decision。
- `evidence/memory-ledger.md`：列 baseline、三次 load wave、reject reason、eviction attempt 和結果。
- `docs/session-contract.md`：說明哪些 request 可排隊、可過期、可縮 context，哪些不得中途斷開。
- `tests/active-session-protection.test.ts`：在記憶體不足時，確認候選 policy 先拒絕新長 request，而不是中止 active decode。

最值得展示的反例是一個「看似能塞進」的 request：不留 output reservation 時它會中途失敗；加上 contract 後它被誠實地排隊或轉 route。

## 延伸閱讀

[混合 prefill／decode 要共用 budget](/zh-HK/interview-lab/mixed-prefill-decode-needs-a-shared-budget)、[model architecture 的速度與容量取捨](/zh-HK/articles/modern-attention-moe-and-serving-tradeoffs) 和 [inference memory、scheduling 與 serving engine 的取捨](/zh-HK/articles/inference-memory-scheduling-and-serving-engines)。

## 範圍說明

這是 AI.DOG 的單題練習。memory ledger、session、token cap、policy、artefact 和結果全是虛構 synthetic 本地草稿材料；不歸屬任何公司，亦不代表任何公司現時或過去的面試流程、live system 或 production outcome。

body.en:
> Interviewer asks: A long-context assistant occasionally runs out of memory. One person proposes clearing the KV cache more aggressively; another wants a larger context cap because users dislike truncation. How would you design a capacity contract?
>
> Half-right answer: KV cache consumes memory, so delete old cache entries. If someone really needs a long context, add more GPU memory.

This answer sees the memory bottleneck but treats the cache like a rubbish bin. A **KV cache** stores the attention keys and values calculated for tokens already read, so the model does not reprocess the full context for every next-token decode. That trades memory for speed. It also means that every long request still being served occupies device memory. The footprint grows with tokens, layers, head size, precision, and concurrent active sessions. The question is not whether cache exists; it is how much each request class may reserve and when a request must not be admitted.

## Promise usable capacity first

A capacity contract is not a sentence such as “N users maximum.” It is a promise the scheduler can enforce: memory reserved for model weights, estimated input tokens plus reserved output tokens for each request class, headroom retained under ordinary load, sessions eligible for idle expiry, active decodes that must not be evicted, and the route used when admission fails. Admission without output reservation can lie to you: a request begins successfully, then OOMs during generation and may disrupt people who were already receiving a reply.

Separate request classes such as short interactions, long-document summaries, and resumable batch work. Give each a context cap, maximum output, deadline, and acceptable substitute route. A long document is not automatically entitled to consume all memory. If it can finish asynchronously, it can wait or be processed in smaller context windows. Conversely, evicting an already-active human interaction can erase an answer midstream, a worse experience than a clear “please wait.”

Think of library desks. Every reader’s open books, notes, and laptop need table space; that is an active KV cache. Throwing away the belongings of someone who has not left frees a desk quickly, but that reader must rebuild their work and may lose it. Letting everyone spread unlimited material means nobody new can sit down. The librarian needs reservations, spare desks, absence limits, and a visible waitlist.

## Turn estimation into admission rules

Start with a synthetic memory ledger: available device memory, model weights, runtime overhead, estimated KV demand for each token bucket, and remaining headroom. When a request enters the queue, estimate conservatively from input tokens plus a reserved maximum output. Admit it only when the reservation fits. When it does not, do not force it in: shrink context, queue it, use an asynchronous route, return a known baseline response, or send it to a human workflow. Those routes must appear in the trace.

Then test three pressure cases: many medium sessions decoding together, one extremely long document arriving suddenly, and idle sessions returning at the peak. Record admission rejects, queue time, eviction, OOM, cancellation, recovery cost, TTFT, and completion rate. The aim is not “memory never fills.” It is that active sessions are not arbitrarily interrupted, every rejection has a stated reason, and pressure still leaves a rollback path.

## Boundaries that are easy to miss

Lower precision, paging, or a smarter cache manager may improve capacity, but none replaces a capacity contract. Quantisation may change output quality; paging may change tail latency; eviction can turn a slow problem into a recomputation problem. Without input/output caps, headroom, and reject-or-handoff rules, each technique merely delays the next OOM. That is why “add hardware” is not the first sentence. It becomes an option after traces show which part needs to grow.

## Evidence you could put in a portfolio

Build `kv-cache-capacity-contract` with:

- `fixtures/sessions.jsonl` containing fictional session token buckets, deadlines, async eligibility, and expected output caps.
- `scripts/estimate-capacity.mjs` with explicit assumptions for output reservation, headroom, and admission.
- `evidence/memory-ledger.md` showing a baseline, three load waves, reject reasons, eviction attempts, and outcomes.
- `docs/session-contract.md` explaining which requests can queue, expire, or shrink context, and which must not be interrupted.
- `tests/active-session-protection.test.ts` that confirms a low-memory policy rejects a new long request before stopping an active decode.

A useful counterexample is a request that appears to fit: without output reservation it fails halfway through; with the contract it is honestly queued or routed elsewhere.

## Further reading

[Mixed prefill and decode traffic needs one budget](/en/interview-lab/mixed-prefill-decode-needs-a-shared-budget), [modern model architecture speed and capacity trade-offs](/en/articles/modern-attention-moe-and-serving-tradeoffs), and [inference memory, scheduling, and serving-engine trade-offs](/en/articles/inference-memory-scheduling-and-serving-engines).

## Scope note

This is an AI.DOG standalone practice prompt. The memory ledger, sessions, token caps, policies, artefacts, and results are fictional synthetic local-draft material. No company is attributed, and this is not evidence of any company’s current or past interview process, a live system, or a production outcome.
